settingsNetwork.announced.heading: What this server announces
settingsNetwork.announced.name: Name
settingsNetwork.announcement.announcing: Slicers and apps on this network can find this server.
settingsNetwork.announcement.failed: This server could not announce itself on the network. The server log says why.
settingsNetwork.announcement.hidden: This server announces nothing, so slicers and apps on this network do not list it.
settingsNetwork.announcement.off: Announcing is switched off in the configuration file, so this setting changes nothing until it is switched on.
settingsNetwork.bridged.body: This server runs in a container on a bridge network, so no other device on your network hears it. Set network_mode: host in compose, or hostNetwork: true in Kubernetes.
settingsNetwork.bridged.title: The announcement stays inside the container
settingsNetwork.hidden.label: Hide this server
settingsNetwork.hidden.note: A hidden server stops announcing itself. Its page and its API still answer at its address, and the sign-in still protects them.
settingsNetwork.timeServer.failed: The operating system would not open UDP port {port}, so the time server is not answering.
settingsNetwork.timeServer.failedInUse: Another program on this computer, such as another time server, holds UDP port {port}. Stop it, then switch the time server on again.
settingsNetwork.timeServer.failedPermiss: This server may not open UDP port {port}. On Linux a program needs a special right to open a port below 1024.
settingsNetwork.timeServer.heading: Time server
settingsNetwork.timeServer.label: Answer the time on this network
settingsNetwork.timeServer.note: Devices that cannot reach the internet, such as cameras, can set their clock from this server. It answers with the clock of the computer it runs on, so keep that clock right.
settingsNetwork.timeServer.off: This server does not answer the time.
settingsNetwork.timeServer.serving: Devices on this network can ask this server for the time on UDP port {port}.
settingsNetwork.title: Network
